title: BitMart exchange to shut down after nine years, BMX token falls 58%
dek: Cryptocurrency exchange BitMart announced an orderly wind-down of its trading platform, halting all trading by August 26, 2026 and ceasing operations on January 31, 2027. The platform's native BMX token fell 58% in 24 hours following the announcement, despite the exchange still clearing $1.6 billion in 24-hour trading volume.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: BitMart stopped accepting new registrations, deposits and trading orders starting July 27, 2026, with all trading ending August 26 and final operations on January 31, 2027.
bottom_line: Watch for completion of the phased closure timeline and any regulatory filings explaining the shutdown rationale. The key metric is whether compliance friction during the six-month wind-down period delays user withdrawals or triggers additional platform stress. The pattern of major exchange exits in a single week suggests sector-wide pressure worth monitoring across remaining platforms.
body: BitMart, a cryptocurrency exchange that has operated for nine years, announced an orderly wind-down of its platform with a phased closure schedule spanning six months.

The exchange stopped accepting new registrations, deposits and new trading orders starting July 27, 2026 at 01:30 UTC on Sunday, according to CoinDesk reporting. All spot and derivatives trading ends on August 26, 2026, while the platform formally ceases operations on January 31, 2027. Withdrawals remain open throughout the wind-down period, though the exchange warned that processing could stretch if request volumes spike.

The platform attributed the closure to "operating conditions, market environment, and future strategic direction," without elaboration. BitMart reported approximately $1.6 billion in 24-hour trading volume prior to the closure announcement, with volume up 51% from the previous period and bitcoin accounting for nearly half of it. Futures accounts moved to reduce-only mode immediately upon announcement.

BitMart's native BMX token fell to approximately 8 cents, down 58% over 24 hours following the announcement, according to CoinDesk. The token's market value dropped to roughly $27 million. The BMX token had already lost approximately 70% of its value over the past year before Sunday's announcement.

Users seeking to withdraw funds will face additional compliance review, including identity verification, device and IP checks, withdrawal-address screening, source-of-funds questions and sanctions checks. The exchange warned that withdrawal processing could extend if request volumes increase during the wind-down period.

BitMart suffered a $196 million hot-wallet breach in December 2021, which the exchange covered at the time. The closure announcement came the same week that BitMEX, a derivatives exchange that operated for 11 years, announced its own shutdown, signaling continued consolidation and operational stress across the exchange sector.
